clue.text: Driver and creator of great cycle rounding turn

indicators.note: to round something is to go around it, so the composer's name encloses the other piece

parts.note: Richard Wagner composed the Ring cycle, a sequence of four operas
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: A driver who is also the composer of a vast operatic cycle, steering round a bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' and 'cycle' suggest transport, but the cycle is Wagner's Ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A waggoner is a person who drives a horse-drawn wagon, an old sense of driver.

clue.text: Asian animal, not European, is seen in river

indicators.note: the European letter is not there, so it is dropped from the animal

parts.note: the tiger is native to Asia
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Asian creature, absent from Europe, turns up by a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tigris is one of the two great rivers of Mesopotamia, flowing through Turkey and Iraq.

clue.text: Supporter joining tribe before match in lively dance

indicators.note: the tribe comes before the word for match, setting the order of the last two pieces

parts.note: a fan supports a team
Dan was one of the twelve tribes of Israel
to go with something is to match it, as colours go together

explanation.surface: A fan joins a group before a game, dancing about excitedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a sporting fixture, but it is the verb, as in colours that go together.
explanation.definitionFit: The fandango is a lively Spanish courtship dance in triple time, often with castanets.

clue.text: Prodigal son immersed?

parts.note: to be immersed is to be in water; the son's letter is put in that word, so the one word gives both the container and the placing
S is the genealogy abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Is the prodigal son, notorious for wasting his inheritance, being baptised?
explanation.walkthrough: The word for water is not written in the clue; 'immersed' supplies both the idea of water and the placing of the son inside it, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A waster is someone who squanders money, exactly what the prodigal son in the parable does.

clue.text: No 1 story from part of India

definitions.note: a noun phrase for a person: the goalkeeper traditionally wears the number 1 shirt

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
a story is a lie, as in 'don't tell stories'

explanation.surface: The best tale comes from a region of India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Story from' reads as source of a tale, but the Indian state simply comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In football and hockey the goalkeeper traditionally wears the number one shirt.

clue.text: Evil overthrown, with good getting on top, holding a sword

indicators.note: in a down clue the good letter sits on top of everything else
the reversed word holds the A inside it
something overthrown is turned upside down, so in a down clue the word evil is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Evil is defeated and good triumphs, all thanks to a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A glaive is an old word for a broadsword, also a pole weapon with a blade.

clue.text: Samurai sword found in trunk at an armoury

indicators.note: the answer is found inside these consecutive words

parts.note: the sword's name runs across these words, from the K of trunk to the first A of armoury

explanation.surface: A Japanese blade is discovered in a chest at an arsenal.
explanation.definitionFit: The katana is the long curved single-edged blade carried by Japanese samurai.

clue.text: Rearrange coat in either half of suitcase

definitions.note: a noun: both 'suit' and 'case' mean a lawsuit

indicators.note: the letters of these two words are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to repack a coat in one side of a suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suitcase' seems to be luggage, but split it: both suit and case mean legal proceedings.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action is a lawsuit, and each half of the luggage word names one.

clue.text: Feelings silly person is hiding in one unpublished work

indicators.note: the jumbled words hide inside the other pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MS is a manuscript, a work not yet in print

indicators.note: silly suggests muddled, so the letters of these words are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An unpublished writer conceals a foolish character in a manuscript, revealing emotions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly person' looks like a fool such as a twit, but 'silly' acts on 'person is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Impressions are feelings or opinions formed about something, as in 'my impression was'.

clue.text: Rage after husband produces something unwearable from wardrobe

indicators.note: the word for rage comes after the husband's letter

parts.note: rage and anger are synonyms

explanation.surface: A furious husband pulls out clothes he would never wear.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like a hideous garment; it is the thing clothes hang on.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat hanger lives in a wardrobe but is not a garment, so it cannot be worn.

clue.text: Ponder, as referee, about extra time

indicators.note: the mediating word goes about, enclosing, the extra letter

parts.note: to mediate is to act as a referee between parties
an extra T for time, added to the mediating word

explanation.surface: A referee thinks hard while playing extra time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extra time' sounds like football; here it is just an additional T.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate is to think deeply or contemplate, the same as to ponder.

clue.text: Part of range seen after symphonist's fifth?

indicators.note: the answer is what is seen after that point in the composer's name

parts.note: Beethoven wrote nine symphonies
everything up to and including the fifth letter of the composer's name is removed

explanation.surface: An oven appears after Beethoven's Fifth Symphony?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Symphonist's fifth' suggests the famous Fifth Symphony, but it means the fifth letter of his name; what follows it is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen range is a cooking stove, and an oven forms part of it.

clue.text: Satire, oddly, about stable employee in secure accommodation

indicators.note: take the odd-numbered letters of the word satire

parts.note: its first, third and fifth letters are kept
on means about, concerning
a groom looks after horses in a stable

explanation.surface: Satire about a stablehand lands someone in a locked room.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongroom is a fortified room for keeping valuables safe, a secure space.

clue.text: Duel as result of rant or challenges like this, with second intervening

definitions.note: a verb: to duel is to fight with swords

indicators.note: the extra letter intervenes, coming between the two halves

parts.words: result of rant or challenges like this
parts.note: cross words are angry words after a rant, and crosswords are puzzles like this one

explanation.surface: A rant leads to a duel, much as puzzles like this provoke conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase gives two readings of the same letters: angry words, or puzzles like this.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross swords is the idiom for fighting a duel, or arguing with someone.

clue.text: Curved weapon — I'm covering it in something left after battle

indicators.note: the two pieces go inside the mark

parts.note: a scar is a mark left by a wound

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece covers another by sitting on top of it

parts.note: taken as written, minus the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A curved blade, which I'm wrapping in a war relic.
explanation.definitionFit: A scimitar is a short sword with a curved blade, associated with the Middle East.

clue.text: Make light of being out of order and try to land

parts.note: a system that is down is not working
an angler plays a fish to tire it before landing it

explanation.surface: A pilot plays down a broken system while attempting to land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try to land' suggests a plane; it is angling, where you play a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To downplay something is to minimise or treat it as less important.

clue.text: For legal reasons, conceal bloody deed

parts.note: red is the colour of blood
an act is a deed

explanation.surface: A legal cover-up of a violent crime.
explanation.definitionFit: To redact is to black out parts of a document, often to avoid legal or security problems.

clue.text: Spanish article raised in kerfuffle? Sword and where it's made

indicators.note: the raised article goes inside the fuss

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word reverses it

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A fuss over a Spanish item: a blade and its place of manufacture.
explanation.walkthrough: Kerfuffle and to-do are both British words for a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo in Spain has long been famous for its steel, and a Toledo is a blade forged there.

clue.text: The box containing novelties I repacked

indicators.note: the letters are packed again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A box of trinkets that I have repacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The box' is British slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: The box is a colloquial name for a TV set, from its old cabinet shape.

clue.text: Run out of passage in bar

indicators.note: the run is taken out of the passage

parts.note: an excerpt is a passage from a text
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A sprint out of a corridor into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' reads as a pub or rod, but it is the preposition, as in 'all bar one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bar used as a preposition means apart from, as in 'everyone bar me'.

clue.text: Kingdom certainly not without king

indicators.note: in its older sense of outside, so the refusal sits outside the king's letter

parts.note: 'no way' is an emphatic refusal
R is from rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A realm that is definitely not without a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway is a constitutional monarchy, so it is literally a kingdom.

clue.text: Call to stop article by multinational medical group

indicators.note: the article is placed by the health body, after it

parts.note: the WHO is the World Health Organization
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An international health body calls a halt over a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoa is the cry used to halt a horse, and more widely to tell someone to slow down.

clue.text: Predator concealing most of his weapon

indicators.note: the bird conceals the shortened word inside it

parts.note: a falcon is a bird of prey

indicators.note: drop the last letter of the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hunter hides almost all of his arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A falchion is a broad, slightly curved medieval sword.

clue.text: Repair broken fencing tool

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: the six letters of this word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mend a damaged tool used on fences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fencing tool' suggests garden fences; it is the sport of fencing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender, sharp-pointed sword used for thrusting in swordplay.

clue.text: Highly formal attire that's used outside work

indicators.note: the first word is used outside, around, the work

parts.note: taken as the word that, with 'is' read as part of the instruction
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Very formal clothing that is worn outdoors at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly' is doing double duty: the hat is tall and the dress formal.
explanation.definitionFit: A top hat is a tall silk hat worn with morning dress or white tie, the most formal attire.

clue.text: American people taking old islander from East to West

indicators.note: an across answer is normally read west to east, so this reads it backwards

parts.note: a Javan is someone from Java

explanation.surface: Americans take in a former islander travelling westward.
explanation.definitionFit: The Navajo are a Native American nation of the south-western United States.
